components.actualCaller: Source processor scheduling calls process_44 for both layerless and layered nodes, and process_43 for layered nodes after layering; CMP_COMBINED dispatch is side comparator then fixed-constraint comparator. Parent driver owns scheduling integration.
branches: Side-fixed node retains known side; only undefined sides use portDummy EXT_PORT_SIDE or netflow. FREE/UNDEFINED node assigns all ports from dummy/netflow then writes FIXED_SIDE.

Netflow is incoming count minus outgoing count, including reversed/current work edges; negative chooses EAST, zero/nonnegative WEST. This differs from realDegree ordering, which excludes REVERSED edges.

FIXED_ORDER/FIXED_RATIO/FIXED_POS sort CMP_COMBINED. First compare N/E/S/W ordinal. Only FIXED_ORDER uses PORT_INDEX when both boxed properties are non-null; explicit integer0 is present. If index compare ties or one is absent, compare positions clockwise: N x ascending, E y ascending, S x descending, W y descending.
FREE/UNDEFINED constraint performs no sort. FIXED_SIDE sorts sides, invokes source reverseWestAndSouthSide literal range/reversal, then optional PORT_DEGREE stable sort.

findPortSideRange intentionally retains source stale-low read and last-index high value; reverse_2 treats high as exclusive and does nothing for range length<=2. Existing implementation already preserves this source behavior; do not repair it by intuition.
PORT_DEGREE only compares same-side E and W. EAST descending non-reversed outgoing degree; WEST ascending non-reversed incoming degree; NORTH/SOUTH/equal values retain stable input order.
Cache construction starts NORTH at0, writes nonempty completed spans then final span even for empty port list; no artificial required-side entries.
Fixed position comparator uses Double total ordering: signed zero is distinguished and NaN sorts after numeric values. The native host numerical adapter must preserve these scalar semantics.

unchangedMappings: Existing source stable sort semantics; Python stable list.sort adapter
helpers.newScalarAdapter: compare_3 is generated java.lang.Double comparison. Use a small original Python IEEE scalar adapter, not copy the GWT runtime; retain this helper provenance and review applicable Apache/GWT attribution separately from ELK kernels.

components.scope: Real node-label location/assignment dispatch, source containers and atomic port-label areas, initial padding/port-border-offset padding, outside node-label container placement and computed node padding. Uses supplied label position/size; does not measure text or claim port-label overlap removal/full pipeline support.
branchFacts: Location declaration has 21 actual locations plus UNDEFINED, assigned-placement set equality controls dispatch. H_PRIORITY changes outside-side selection; no nearest/default location is invented when placement does not match.

The label-specific NODE_LABELS_PLACEMENT property uses presence rather than truthiness: explicit empty set overrides node placement and resolves UNDEFINED. onlyInside filters real outside locations. Real LabelCell mode is direction supplied, not one forced visual arrangement.
Inside Grid is inserted into the middle horizontal Strip CENTER with nodeLabelsPadding. Outside N/S horizontal and W/E vertical Strips have only their actual edge-facing nodeLabelSpacing padding.
Node label cells are cached by location; outside N/S contribute height before full sizing constraints while E/W contribute width. Inside/outside flags are not globally enabled by creator.

Port label areas are true AtomicCell regions, distinct from per-port actual LabelCell; W/E label width can grow the region only for INSIDE. N/S spacingVertical is copied only when >=0; surrounding-port margins preserve supplied 0 and signed values.

Node-border padding first uses negative explicit border offset. Fixed port-label geometry additionally computes inside part via real label bounds and side, then symmetric opposite padding follows literal source additions of signed border offset.

Computed padding is gated by COMPUTE_PADDING and calculated from actual node cell and Grid center rectangles. Outside placement consumes current dimensions/overhang and performs actual Strip child layout; no text estimation or fake client rect.
Full constrained/unconstrained per-port LabelCell positioning and overlap removal are separate pending source blocks, needed before process orchestration can be declared complete.

components.scope: Actual simple/constrained port LabelCell placement and RectangleStripOverlapRemover algorithm, using already created contexts/cells and supplied labels. No new node/count/label constraint, no text measurement, no graph kernel admission claim.
branchFacts: Constrained selection is !PORT_LABELS sizeConstraint OR FIXED_POS; INSIDE takes precedence over OUTSIDE. Missing/unpositioned LabelCell is skipped without resetting first-special state until a real label is placed.

N/S constrained placement performs real rectangle-strip overlap removal; E/W delegates to simple. Outside constrained only runs beyond2ports, preserving literal threshold as an algorithm branch, not an admitted port-count cap.

UP/DOWN preserve original rectangle identity on import. UP exports start-height-y, DOWN adds start to the same mutated y. LEFT/RIGHT use a transformed temporary rectangle and copy back only original x.

Initial rectangle list is GWT P02S actual comparator sort by left border; overlap lists use List.sort_0 -> same approved mergeSort. Double comparator is existing original IEEE native adapter, not copied GWT Double runtime.

Scanline active TreeSet is comparator-keyed by right border, not object identity: equal right border replaces only value, retaining the first node key. Active iteration is ascending right border; touching horizontal bounds overlap because expiry uses strict <.

Native active collection may use an ordered comparator-unique list preserving these exact observable semantics. No TreeMap rotation/runtime code is copied. AlreadyPlaced HashSet is membership-only and native object identity is sufficient; no iteration-order assumption.

Greedy processes actual initial rectangle order, sorts overlaps by their current y, moves against only already placed rectangles with two strict inequalities and gap, then returns max bottom. No graph-size cap or different packer substitute.

Constrained inside uses ElkMath.maxd rather than Math.max: source starts at fixed intern126 and updates only >, so NaN elements do not poison a finite maximum. Other arithmetic uses real JS min/max adapters with NaN and signed-zero behavior.
LabelCell source alignment and group/first-label size behavior remain real C05/C07; applying staged LabelCell geometry and global label output is a later caller, not invented by this module.

horizontalLayoutMode defaults true unless supplied graph explicitly has direction; then only UNDEFINED/LEFT/RIGHT are horizontal. Global graph direction absence differs from a present UP/DOWN value.

Source exact order: minimum center, border padding, H/V placement minima, contributions, width, H ports, N/S labels, vertical padding update, height. Do not calculate height before the N/S label overlap stage.

When applyStuff=false, return staged nodeSize immediately after height, without SOUTH offset, V ports, final labels, node size/padding/position writes. Existing scratch volatile ids are still assigned earlier.

Apply path runs SOUTH offset, V ports, E/W labels, outside N/S then E/W containers, node LabelCell apply in original enum-key order, port LabelCell apply in real context order, computed padding, actual node size coordinate-copy, final staged port coordinate-copy.
